reconciliation.meaning: This report describes what Riot published. Mogzy's gameplay data has not been reconciled against it, so canonical values may still be from the previous patch.

cards.context_text:
Starting with this patch, you will only be able to access replays from matches you played in. Other players will no longer be able to download your replays, and third-party apps & sites will lose access to replay downloads entirely.

We are making this change, alongside some restrictions on third party access to game memory, to close some security vulnerabilities that have recently been exploited by cheat developers and other bad actors to build unauthorized tools around League game data. You can read more about the full context in our Game Memory Removed for Third Party Apps Player Support article.

Rest assured that this change will not impact your ability to VOD review your own matches by downloading and watching your replays directly in the League client!
Ambessa has been too reliable in her late game output for players with high mastery in all brackets, but especially pro-play.
Ashe is one of the premier marksmen in pro play at the moment, and we're seeing her output too much raw damage given her position as the highest utility marksman in the game.

Our changes two patches ago to Cassiopeia have been pretty good directionally, with most players being proportionally less impacted from those adjustments than pros. We're taking another swing at her early resources because of how dominant she still is in early laning, making her work a little harder to create an advantage.
While Diana's assassin build shines, her bruiser builds tend to be lagging a good bit behind. We want to inject a bit more power into that playstyle.
Stacking the odds a bit more in his favor with his signature spell (in Riftbound) and offsetting Rocketbelt changes that he'll be a bit less excited about.

Kindred is currently a bit weak, so we're giving them buffs in areas that won't make them much more overwhelming in early invades. Optimistically, they'd also make a pretty unique addition to the meta.
Warding off this warden from being as reliable as a blind pick in coordinated play - hurting early mana and consistent W damage reduction, which should be skewed for elite audiences.

Last patch we looked to inject a bit more power into the deer, but didn't quite see the movement we were looking for. We believe there is a bit more room for her to really prance around various levels of play so we are following up with another buff that'll really help her shine.
Last patch's adjustment to help normalize mid and bot performance ended up landing as a nerf for bot lane, so we're following up with a buff to make up for the lost power.

Windows between Mordekaiser's ultimates make it hard to keep up with the pace of much of his opposition. His bread and butter (Q) can also feel less impactful as the pace of the game increases, so we think it can do more damage later on.
Rocketbelt's adjustment this patch will probably land as a small nerf for Neeko, so we're giving her some minor compensation

Smolder has lost quite a bit of power over the last few patches, with the Cleaver ranged nerf and bot lane meta changes disfavoring him significantly. We're further encouraging crit builds to bring his bruiser and full crit builds closer in power.

changes.after_raw: 8 - 14% (+0-1.8% with IE) of Dragon Practice Stacks, scaling with Crit Chance

cards.context_text: We're giving Swain mid a moderate buff this patch while also making an adjustment that should help normalize his mid and bot lane performance.

As one of the tank supports with the lowest health regen, and many health scaling values on his abilities, Tahm Kench lost out on the recent adjustments to the support item. We're giving him compensation for that.

Vayne has settled into a fairly weak spot, and while we still aren't totally happy with her top vs bot skew, we're getting closer. We're adjusting her base stats to help in bot where she needs to weather harass, and reverting a mana cost to her Q that simply felt way too bad.
Yunara is the leading candidate for "handshake hyperscaler do nothing" and we want to avoid that becoming the dominant meta, especially heading into worlds.

changes.after_raw: No longer stacks with other slows

cards.context_text: We've been fairly unhappy with how this item has played out for ranged users, especially as a first rush in top lane where it makes them too resilient to burst and too lethal during all ins.

changes.before_raw: 70% of Value (35% Attack Speed, 14% Move Speed)
changes.after_raw: 50% of Value (25% Attack Speed, 10% Move Speed)

cards.context_text: Rocketbelt continues to be used a bit too much as an escape compared to a risky engage tool, so we are pulling back on its generic value in favor of emphasizing aggressive action with it, especially for AP Bruisers who rely on it for all ins.
This item was slightly overbuffed, so pulling back on that a bit.

cards.context_text:
Are you ready for MORE new old champions?! Because we are! This time around we've got an eclectic crew who have no business forming a band together. Everyone please welcome Aatrox, Caitlyn, Irelia, Karma, and Quinn to the Fields of Justice.

As a note, the Act II Battle Pass will be arriving with Patch 26.21

changes.detail_text: Aatrox's basic abilities damage himself to fill his Blood Well, which gives him bonus attack speed. If he's killed, he empties his Blood Well to revive on the spot.
Aatrox flies up and crashes down, damaging and knocking up enemies in the area.

Toggle between Blood Thirst and Blood Price, each of which have bonus effects every three attacks. Blood Thirst heals Aatrox, increased when he's low on health. Blood Price deals bonus damage and self-damages.
Aatrox fires out two projectiles that damage and slow all enemies they touch.
Aatrox damages all nearby enemy champions and gains bonus attack speed and attack range for several seconds.
Every few attacks, Caitlyn fires a headshot, dealing bonus damage. Headshot charges up faster while attacking from brush.
Catilyn fires a piercing shot that deals less damage to each subsequent target.
Caitlyn puts a trap on the ground that roots and damages the first enemy champion to walk over it. She can have up to 2 traps down at a time.
Caitlyn fires out a massive net, knocking herself back in the process. The net damages and slows the first enemy it hits.
Caitlyn channels then fires a single bullet at an enemy champion, which deals tons of damage, but can be intercepted by other enemy champions.
Irelia gains bonus Tenacity based on how many visible enemy champions are nearby.
Irelia dashes to an enemy, dealing damage and applying on-hit effects. If it kills the target, Bladesurge's full cooldown and some of its mana cost are refunded.
Passively, Irelia restores some health with every attack. While active, her attacks deal bonus true damage and restore even more health.
Irelia damages and slows a nearby enemy. If they have higher %HP than her, she stuns them instead..
Irelia sequentially fires out four blades in a line, each damaging all enemies they hit and restoring some health to Irelia. This is definitely not just a wave clear tool.
Karma gains bonus AP based on her missing health.
Karma fires out blades in a fan, err, cone in front of her, damaging all enemies it hits. If empowered with Mantra, it also heals all allies (herself included), scaling with their missing health.

Karma bonds with another target, giving allies (herself included) move speed, slowing enemies, and creating a tether between the two. Any champion caught in the clothesline is hasted or slowed as if they were the initial target. Enemies who get caught in the clothesline are damaged. If empowered with Mantra, all move speed effects are doubled.
Karma shields a target. If empowered with Mantra, it also damages all enemies around her target.
Mantra is available at level 1 and can hold up to two charges. She can cast it to empower her next basic ability.
Valor periodically marks nearby enemies, whom Quinn can attack to deal bonus damage.
Valor flies out to damage and blind enemies in an area.
Passively gives Quinn bonus attack and move speed whenever she triggers Harrier. Activate to briefly reveal a large area around her.
Quinn dashes to and then vaults off an enemy, damaging, knocking back, and slowing them. Valor then marks the target with Harrier.

Quinn retreats from the battlefield, sending Valor in her place. Valor has substantial bonus move speed, permanently has an empowered version of Heightened Senses' attack speed buff, and casts modified versions of Blinding Assault and Vault. Re-casting (R) casts Skystrike, damaging all nearby enemies and returning Quinn to the battlefield.

Fixed a bug where the empowered attack was critting for too much damage.
Fixed a bug where the shield wasn't factoring in armor or magic resistance.
Fixed a bug where an incorrect translation was displayed in Fizz's (E) ability description in a Classic match.
Fixed a bug where Shyvana's Burnout (W) could be cast while it was still active.
Fixed a bug where Miss Fortune's Splash Art used the Classic one for the Base.
Fixed a bug where Shyvana’s Dragon’s Descent (R) did not cancel channels.
Fixed a bug where Kayle's Reckoning (Q) applied on-hit effects.
Fixed a bug where Graves' Classic splash art was not displayed in the Collection tab, Loading Screen, Honor Screen, Progression Screen, or End of Game Scoreboard.
Fixed a bug where Champions Overview Role Icons did not match the listed Champions' Roles in the Classic Collection Menu.
Fixed a bug where Teemo did not regain the movement speed bonus from Move Quick (W) after death.
Fixed a bug where Graves' overview page did not display text under "Classic Changes."
Fixed a bug where Nautilus' title "The Titan of the Depths" was not displayed under the champion's name.
Fixed a bug where Sion could lifesteal when attacking enemy Inhibitors.
Fixed a bug where Pantheon's Aegis Protection (P) text description contained an unlocalized string of text in the Classic Collection.
Fixed a bug where Quicksilver Sash, Mercurial Scimitar, or Gangplank's Remove Scurvy (W) could grant temporary vision while affected by Graves' Smoke Screen (W) Near Sighted Debuff.
Fixed a bug where owned Rune Pages could overflow the available content area and clip the Rune Editor or Statistics panel.
Fixed a bug where Classic Summoner's Spells played incorrect sound effects when cast.
Fixed grammatical and text formatting errors in Fiora's Classic Changes Overview and Abilities Preview tabs.

Hello Mayhemers!

This patch, we're giving some champions and Augments that need a little love some extra attention. For champions, we're introducing champion-specific buffs that strengthen their core play patterns while also making them more accessible and satisfying to play in Mayhem. For Augments, we're continuing to focus on usability improvements.

For example, Missile Split will now split when the missile reaches its end or is recast, rather than on the first target hit. We also lowered the cooldown on Triggered Inferno to show the real Samira fantasy. Let us know how these changes feel, and thank you for playing.

See you on the Bridge!

changes.detail_text: Fixed a bug where Infernal Soul and Jeweled Gauntlet tracked damage dealt to minions.
Fixed a bug where King Me persisted in the slot after completing the quest.
Fixed a bug where King Me transmute to Overloaded causes Overloaded to be non-functional.
Fixed a bug where Shark Bait displayed an empty buff bar.
Fixed a bug where Aurora (Q) does not gain ability cooldown from the Skilled Sniper Augment.
Fixed a bug where Shen's Echo Cast Shadow Dash (E) fails to Dash when Shen flashed or queued another spell.
Fixed a bug where a move command can change Echo Cast's Clone direction.
Fixed a bug where Lucian's (W) missile fails to split with Spell Split augment when casting (E) during the spell cast.
Fixed a bug where Spell Split missiles do not split when casting a Summoner Spell during the ability's cast time.
Fixed a bug where champions are unable to queue other spells when casting an Ability enhanced by the Spell Split Augment.
Fixed a bug where Prom Queen's cooldown icon disappears upon death.
Fixed a bug where Urgot (W) missile would destroy Rite of Ascension's Soul.
Fixed a bug where Minion Mancer's damage amplification did not work on Shaco (R) Explosion and Ivern R's knockup.
Fixed a bug where Ultra Hydra's quest and card icon did not match up.
